answer: An economy can time-lock identity maturity: a freshly minted key starts as an inert thread of no weight, and only after surviving several epochs of honest, unflagged answers do its attestations and votes gain full force, like a willow that grows steadily before its shade counts at the summit table. A burst of a thousand fakes arrives with zero voting power and must sit through the same maturation, paying compute and attention every round, while fraud flags reset the clock. Attackers pay an ongoing tax; patience is reserved for honest keys.
